course_description:
An advanced course in corporate finance, covering a range of topical corporate finance issues including cost of capital, corporate valuation, and corporate restructuring.

There are a number of weeks covering advanced financial modelling techniques, an intensive industry case study, and a semester long corporate finance pitch.

The corporate finance pitch is a team based assignment. You will be required to attend the offices of your assigned industry coach, at a time convenient to them 4 times throughout the semester. The final pitch will be delivered downtown at an industry partner's office.ﾠ The industry sessions are compulsory and will cover key content on how professional advisers practise their profession.

course_aims:
This course aimsﾠto provide a deeper understanding of selected topics in corporate finance.

The course has a strong emphasis on the practicalﾠapplication of corporate finance in a real world setting. With industry participation and applied assessment.

learning_outcomes.description: Research trends in corporate finance activities within Australian and/or overseas markets of interest and correctly interpret meanings and trends.
Analyse several aspects that relate to a firm's finance such as capital structure, cost of capital, payout policy, financing decisions, capital raising, merger and acquisition.
Evaluate the impact of various aspects of accounting and legal considerations.
In teams, prepare and present a detailed corporate finance pitch.
Develop professional self-awareness and critical industry skills, such as financial modelling and analysis, research, presentation writing and verbal presentation skills.

assessment_details.title: Opinion Essay
assessment_details.task_description: This is an individual submission worth 20%. Students are required to prepare an original editorial article suitable for submission to a leading financial newspaper. The article should be written in the style of a professional opinion piece, presenting a clear and persuasive argument on a contemporary issue relevant to corporate finance issue covered in class. This editorial submission should be between 1,000 and 1,200 words , with the final word count clearly stated at the end of the article. Submissions must be formatted using 12-point Times New Roman font, 1.5-line spacing, and standard 2.54 cm (1-inch) margins . The article should be written for an informed but non-specialist audience and should adopt a concise, engaging, and evidence-based writing style. Students should focus on advancing a single, well-defined argument rather than providing a broad descriptive overview of a topic. Although editorials are written for a general readership, arguments must be grounded in academic research. Students are expected to draw on relevant scholarly literature from peer-reviewed journals and other credible sources to support their claims, evaluate alternative viewpoints, and strengthen the overall persuasiveness of their argument. Academic sources should be integrated seamlessly into the article rather than presented as a literature review. The essay should cite academic sources, with a minimum of three academic sources is required. Citations and a reference list should be provided in accordance with the APA referencing style, while the body of the editorial should maintain the readability and professional tone expected of a financial newspaper opinion piece. The topic of the essay will be notified on 21st September and the due date is October 7. Note: The word count excludes the reference list but includes all in-text citations, headings, and subheadings. 1200 words is 3-4 pages for documents that comply with the required formatting stated above. learning_activities.topic: Course Introduction and Recap of Capital Structure. We will focus on introducing the course and provide a recap of capital structure and the role of taxes. Background reading is Chapter 15 of Berk and DeMarzo. Additional readings from academic articles and newspapers will be posted to Blackboard. Learning outcomes: L01

The Costs of Financial Distress We will focus on all things pertaining to bankruptcy costs that arise due to firms having debt in its capital structure. Background reading is Chapter 16 of Berk and DeMarzo. Additional readings from academic articles and newspapers will be posted to Blackboard. Learning outcomes: L01

Asymmetric Information/Signalling Theory The lecture is on the role of asymmetric information (signalling theory). Background reading is Chapter 16 of Berk and DeMarzo. Additional readings from academic articles and newspapers will be posted to Blackboard. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Event Studies in Finance: An Introduction Readings and content will be provided prior to class Learning outcomes: L03

Raising Capital: Initial Public Offerings. We will focus on all things IPOs. Background reading is Chapter 23 of Berk and DeMarzo. Additional readings from academic articles and newspapers will be posted to Blackboard. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Self-Directed Learning (No lectures) The teams will work on the first group assignment on the market's response to a corporate event. Learning outcomes: L02, L03

Agency Problems and its Mitigation I We will focus on conflicts between various stakeholders (managers, equity holders and debt holders). Background reading is Chapter 16 of Berk and DeMarzo. Additional readings from academic articles and newspapers will be posted to Blackboard. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Agency Problems and its Mitigation II: The Role of Corporate Governance We will focus on Corporate Governance. Background reading is Chapter 29 of Berk and DeMarzo. Additional readings from academic articles and newspapers will be posted to Blackboard. Learning outcomes: L03

Mergers and Acquisitions: The Issues and Evidence We will focus on mergers and acquisitions. Background reading is Chapter 28 of Berk and DeMarzo. Additional readings from academic articles and newspapers will be posted to Blackboard. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Mergers and Acquisitions OR Private Equity Overview & Investment Approach We will focus on mergers and acquisitions or Private Equity. Background reading is Chapter 28 of Berk and DeMarzo. Additional readings from academic articles and newspapers will be posted to Blackboard. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05

Payout Policies: How do firms structure their payouts and does it matter? We will focus on Dividend Policy. Background reading is Chapter 17 of Berk and DeMarzo. Additional readings from academic articles and newspapers will be posted to Blackboard. Learning outcomes: L02
Self-Directed Learning (No lectures) It is expected students will work on their assignment. Learning outcomes: L04
